messages.subject: Re: robots.txt on shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: robots.txt on shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
robots.txt are not currently customizable.
We found that web crawlers would trigger sleeping applications to start, but not necessarily wait for them to load, nor make use of SockJS to interact with the application in order to render the contents, so there was no value being added.
Additionally, since robots.txt must exist at the top-level of the domain, i.e. myaccount.shinyapps.io/robots.txt <http://myaccount.shinyapps.io/robots.txt>, they would need to be configured at the account level, not per application.
We have on our backlog to see about supporting serving something static to the web crawlers so that applications can be indexed, but this is not currently scheduled work.

messages.subject: Re: Authentication system with persistent data storage for multiple users
messages.subject_clean: Authentication system with persistent data storage for multiple users
messages.body_plain:
There is no persistent storage provided with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> today, although it is something we are actively pursuing.
All plans allow your application to access persistent storage <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/Storage.html> you have elsewhere though.

> I am currently involved in a project where I am creating a machine learning flashcard application, and plan to use shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. The application will be tested in a class, with multiple students trialing the application.
>
> Is it possible to create an authentication system with shiny where each student can create an account, and their progress will be stored in a specific database (eg. mysql, dropbox etc), so when they re-login, they will continue where they left off? Basically, storing data for each user in a database, and then querying the information for that specific user. My approach would be to store user information in a cookie, and then use that information to query the database.
>
> Is it possible to do this in the lowest paid ($9/month) shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> package? Does this package allow me to store persistent data, read cookies, and ultimately create an authentication system for different users?
>
> Thanks for your time.
>

messages.body_plain:
The documentation gives a slightly longer explanation <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/applications.html#worker-settings>, but is essentially the same.
The connection timeout looks at traffic in both directions, while the read timeout is the application reading from the browser, thus if you have a dashboard you want to set that to 0.

The higher you set the timeouts, the more hours your application will consume, so make sure you are on an appropriate plan.

messages.body_plain:
Hi

I'm trying to make a multi-user Shiny application.
I haven't been working with Shiny that long, so I don't have a lot of experience.
I want the users to log in with their own Google account, so the app uses their own data to retrieve information from Google Analytics and BigQuery.
I've been using googleAuthR and the authentication works perfectly on my localhost and retrieves all the info from GA and BigQuery as expected, but when I deploy it to https://my.shinyapps.io/myApp/ I get the following error as soon as I login:
JSON fetch error: Invalid Credentials

> 1. The app is deployed to https://my.shinyapps.io/myApp
> 2. I click on the login button
> 3. It prompts me to choose the Google account I want to authenticate with
> 4. I choose the account
> 5. JSON fetch error: Invalid Credentials

I must be missing something or doing something silly, so any help would be appreciated :)

I use googleAnalyticsR and bigrquery to retrieve information from GA and BigQuery.

Abbreviation of what I have so far:

In ui.R I have a shinydashboard using
googleAuthUI("loginButton")

In server.R I use the following logic:
options(googleAuthR.client_id = "myclientID.apps.googleusercontent.com <http://myclientID.apps.googleusercontent.com>")
options(googleAuthR.client_secret = "myClientSecret")
options(googleAuthR.scopes.selected = c("https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics",
                                        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/bigquery"))

options(googleAuthR.webapp.client_id = "myWebClientID.apps.googleusercontent.com <http://myWebClientID.apps.googleusercontent.com>")
options(googleAuthR.webapp.client_secret = "myWebClientSecret")

access_token <- callModule(googleAuth, "loginButton")
data<- reactive({
      data <- with_shiny(google_analytics,
                                     id = viewId,
                                     start=startDate,
                                     end=endDate,
                                     metrics = "ga:goal1Completions",
                                     shiny_access_token = access_token())

})
output$dataBox <- renderValueBox({
      ## only trigger once authenticated
      req(access_token())
      valueBox(
        data()$goal1Completions,
        "My goal 1 test data", icon = icon("heartbeat"), color = "blue"
      )
})

In https://console.developers.google.com/apis/

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-CxhmzAsuUng/WH4b1YgzTsI/AAAAAAAAFPU/9-GY5HBb7MIuTfJN9DhjqEJBNYMhOzdtwCLcB/s1600/help1.png>

Any suggestions or insights welcome :)
Thank you

messages.body_plain:
When deploying to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, we use the same version of R and the same package versions that are installed locally.

However, we do attempt to cache the built packages (this can be toggled off/on per application), and there was a recent instance of ggplot2 introducing a build time dependency <https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/7f04c255e0f586fd635cb173b7bedd6a7714cece/cran-comments.md#ggproto-mistake> by mistake which caused the cached ggiraph package to have problems, which was resolved by purging it from the cache to allow it be built against the fixed version of ggplot2. I mention that mainly because of meh256's comment in issue 59 <https://github.com/MarkEdmondson1234/googleAuthR/issues/59#issuecomment-273379714>.

I can't think of a reason that options would have started behaving differently as of December, but I suppose for debugging one could set an option and then either render it or print it and view the logs to verify the value, which worked for me with:

options("googleAuthR.webapp.client_secret" = "something_something")
print(options("googleAuthR.webapp.client_secret"))

Let me know if you think of anything else to try, and I am happy to collaborate in real time to get to the bottom of this mystery.
